verdict:
The synthesis is only partly sound. Most of its prices and renderer facts hold up. Its bake-off does not: the size is wrong, the season breaks the comparison, and the variants are confounded.

**What checked out on 2026-10-17:**
- Calibrite prices: Classic US$99 list / US$74.25 sale; Passport Photo 2 US$119 / US$89.25.
- RunPod: RTX 4090 at US$0.34/h community, US$0.89/h secure, US$1.10/h serverless.
- SpeedTree: Indie US$19/mo, Pro US$899/yr, Library US$999.
- RealityScan: free under US$1M revenue, otherwise US$1,250 per seat per year.
- Maxtree EULA tiers: Indie up to US$100k, Pro up to US$250k, Enterprise above, all on total revenue.
- Maxtree hydrangeas are macrophylla (plus petiolaris) only. There is no Physocarpus, Cornus sericea, H. paniculata or 'Smaragd'. Maxtree's own pages say its low-poly editions are "not suitable for use in games".
- Fab: Boxwood "From $7.05 to $70.70"; Bigleaf Hydrangea and Norway Maple are free; a hosta search finds no hosta.
- PlantCatalog Koster 12/43: CC BY 4.0, 44.7k triangles, "exported at 40%".
- three r185.1 WebGLShadowMap.js:482 forces alphaTest 0.5 under A2C.
- foliageLighting.ts injects its terms at <opaque_fragment>, after outgoingLight is computed.
- photoGrade.ts sets the day sun radius to 0.9 deg.
- RBG professional-photography permits cost $172-375.

**What fails:**
1. The bake-off is roughly 2-3x larger than "6-7 agent-days". Its own variant budgets already add up to 7.5 days before V0's render fixes (3.5 days of P0+P1 plus the synthesis's own 3-5 days) and before the 3-4-day capture chain.
2. In mid-October the bake-off can test owner capture properly only on Smaragd.
3. Rebuilding V3 and V4 to the same caps, with wrong-species stand-ins, means they cannot show a "geometry gap".
4. The proposed idle accumulation reuses code the repo disabled on purpose because of a visible artefact.
5. Maxtree coverage is undercounted: Amelanchier canadensis exists at species level.

The realism scores (6/10 to 9.5/10) are unsupported estimates that I could neither confirm nor refute.

**Checks I could not finish:**
- The web-search budget ran out mid-task. Remaining checks used direct page fetches and the browser pane instead.
- The Xfrog/CGTrader, Superhive search and Globe Plants catalogue pages could not be read.
- Maxtree's per-format and per-tier prices are not shown on the product pages (only "$26 to $368" per species and "$125 to $1,770" per volume), so US$26/78/156 could not be confirmed.

problems.claim: A 'look bake-off' of 6-7 agent-days (bakeoff.effort_days = 7) can be run before committing to the 34.5-day programme or any spend.
problems.problem:
The synthesis's own numbers put the bake-off at roughly 15-25 agent-days before a verdict, not 7. Three things drive this:
- The variant budgets alone already exceed 7 days.
- V0's shared render fixes are prerequisites that are not counted.
- V1 and V2 are priced far below what the plan and the synthesis charge for the same work elsewhere.
problems.evidence:
Variant budgets: V1 2.5 + V2 1.5 + V3 2 + V4 1.5 = 7.5 days.

V0 needs P0 (1.5 d) and P1 (2 d), per PLAN.md lines 47-51. It also needs alpha:false, shader v2, coverage mips, customDepthMaterial, a bed stub, idle accumulation and the Photo-mode transmission and sun changes. The synthesis's own route-1 'time' says these need 'about 3-5 d' on top of P0/P1/P2.

V1 '2.5 agent-days' must prototype P3 hull-and-shell, a P5 shrub with globe heads and a P7 space-colonisation tree, each with LOD1 and LOD2 billboard clouds plus raised stills LOD0. PLAN.md prices P3 (pipeline plus three clipped evergreens) at 7 days. That includes the spec table, sprites and atlas packer, GLB writer, Node rasteriser and CC0 sourcing scripts (PLAN.md lines 881-935). PLAN.md also prices P5 at 4.5 d and P7 at 4.5 d (lines 57-61).

V2's '1.5 agent-days' requires the darktable, BiRefNet, Meshroom and atlas chain. Route 2 prices that chain at 'about 3-4 d'.

problems.fix:
Re-size the bake-off openly:
- V0 = P0 + P1 + the render extras (about 6.5-8.5 d).
- V1 = a cut-down pipeline spike (about 4-6 d, or narrow it to one species).
- V2 = the capture chain (3-4 d).
- V3 and V4: 3-4 d.
- Contact-sheet and judging harness: about 1 d.

Alternatively, shrink the scope to one species (Smaragd) and two or three variants to genuinely hit about 7 days. State calendar time including the owner shoot and review.

problems.claim: The programme is 'the 34.5-day programme'. Owner-captured atlases add 'about 3-4 d', and the render fixes add 'about 3-5 d'.
problems.problem: The verdict's headline figure is understated. The synthesis's own additions make the recommended programme about 47-60+ agent-days, not 34.5.
problems.fix: Give the owner one total: P0-P9 + render extras + capture chain + bake-off, with optional items listed separately. The verdict should not cite '34.5-day' as the cost of the recommended mix.

problems.claim: In the V2 bake-off, owner-captured atlases (shot now) are compared blind against real reference photos for Smaragd, Annabelle and sugar maple. If V2 passes, the rule is to 'adopt route 2 for all 26'.
problems.problem:
In mid-October only Smaragd can be captured in the state DeckCraft renders (green, summer). The decision rule therefore generalises from one evergreen, which the synthesis itself calls 'the easiest atlas of all 26', to 21 deciduous species and their blooms.
- Annabelle's white heads cannot be captured now, and its leaves are turning.
- Real reference photos taken now show autumn states.
- V1 and V3 render white heads; V3 and V4 maples are summer-green.
The blind photo-match is therefore season-mismatched for two of three species.
problems.evidence:
NC State Extension (https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/hydrangea-arborescens/): bloom 'May-July' and 'The leaves turn yellow in fall.'

Ontario Parks fall colour report (https://www.ontarioparks.ca/fallcolour): Bronte Creek, near Burlington and Waterdown, on 14 Oct 2026 shows colour change 60 and leaf fall 30.

The synthesis's own V2 text says that, failing green leaves, the maples are rendered 'in an autumn state' and Annabelle uses 'one approved Gemini/ChatGPT ... sheet'. In that case V2 for Annabelle tests AI, not owner capture.

PLAN.md P5 renders Annabelle with '8-15 white globe heads'.
problems.fix:
Limit this autumn's verdict to clipped evergreens (Smaragd, plus boxwood and yew if added). Either:
- render every variant and reference in a matched autumn state (tan Annabelle heads, autumn maple), or
- defer the deciduous comparison to a June-July 2027 bake-off.
State in the decision rule that adopting route 2 for deciduous species is provisional until summer capture is tested.

problems.claim: V3 (Maxtree) and V4 (Megascans) are rebuilt 'to the same caps as V1' and judged blind beside real photos of Smaragd, Annabelle and sugar maple. 'If V3 or V4 clearly beat V2 while V1/V2 fail, the gap is geometry.'
problems.fix:
Add an uncapped arm:
- render V3 and V4 at source resolution in Photo mode and the desktop still as the true ceiling;
- run the capped rebuild as a separate arm.
Judge V4 against reference photos of its own species (boxwood, H. macrophylla, Norway maple), not the target species, and reword the decision rule accordingly.

problems.claim: Render fix: 'Idle progressive supersampling ... reusing the jitter and blend code in renderPipeline.tsx:75-84 (dead today because SHOWCASE_STILL_SAMPLES=1)'. It 'removes shimmer ... on every tier'.
problems.problem: The code is not accidentally dead. It was disabled on purpose because of a visible artefact, which the synthesis does not address. The existing code is also not a progressive cross-frame accumulator.
problems.fix: Treat idle accumulation as new work: cross-frame accumulation with invalidate-driven continuation under frameloop="demand", reset rules, and depth and DOF consistency. Add an acceptance test on deck stair treads at the Corner and Front cameras. Budget it explicitly rather than calling it reuse.

problems.claim: Maxtree covers 'About 17 at species level', with Amelanchier lamarckii only at genus level. The per-species serviceberry fallback is 'Commission (no species-level stock found)'.
problems.problem: Maxtree sells Amelanchier canadensis, the exact target species, in two volumes. The research searched only species-named product titles and missed volume contents. Species-level coverage is about 18, and serviceberry does not need a commission. C. x acutiflora V109 (no cultivar named; 131-191 cm tall, which matches 'Karl Foerster') is also left out of the coverage count.
problems.evidence:
https://maxtree.org/product/plant-models-vol-181/: Amelanchier canadensis, 6 variants, 66,469-144,487 polys.

https://maxtree.org/product/plant-models-vol-183/: Amelanchier canadensis, 115,305-206,526 polys.

The Maxtree site search for 'amelanchier' (https://maxtree.org/?s=amelanchier&post_type=product) returns Vol 181 and Vol 183 alongside the V94/V144 lamarckii items.

Vol 109: Calamagrostis acutiflora, 9 variants, 591,186-1,686,429 polys.
problems.fix: Correct the count to about 18 at species level. Make serviceberry's paid fallback 'Maxtree Vol 181/183 A. canadensis' and drop the commission. Re-search Maxtree by genus (volume contents are indexed) for every remaining 'not found' species before recommending commissions.

problems.claim: The sugar maple best route uses 'Bark from owner capture or Poly Haven CC0 trident_maple_bark'.
problems.problem: This brings back a texture that the reviewed plan rejected on realism grounds.
problems.evidence: PLAN.md, P7 (line ~1325): 'Bark, procedural only. The trident_maple_bark download is dropped: its flaky, plated bark reads old on a 2.5 in trunk.'
problems.fix: Use owner-captured young sugar-maple bark (smooth grey with lenticels), or the plan's procedural bark. Remove trident_maple_bark as an option.

problems.claim: Photo mode should use 'sun radius 0.265 deg in place of 0.9 deg (photoGrade.ts:26), so penumbrae ... are not 3.4x too soft'.
problems.problem:
The change is presented as a pure correction, but it has costs and gaps:
- The 0.9 deg value is a documented, deliberate choice.
- Golden hour uses 1.45 deg, which the synthesis does not mention.
- sunDisc holds irradiance constant, so shrinking the disc raises sun radiance about 11.5x, which can add fireflies at the fixed 384 spp.
problems.evidence:
src/features/deckcraft/photoGrade.ts (6ba1adf): 'A print-like sun: a little larger than the real 0.27 deg so the penumbra reads in a still ...' and SUN_ANGULAR_RADIUS_DEG = {day:0.9, golden:1.45, night:0}.

sunDisc() computes radiance = irradiance / (pi*tan^2(theta)), and (0.9/0.265)^2 is about 11.5.
problems.fix: Make it a measured A/B in the bake-off at both Day and Golden hour (penumbra width against a reference photo, plus firefly count at 384 spp). Include the golden 1.45 deg value.

problems.claim: The V2 owner capture is 'about 3 h': Smaragd cuttings, green Annabelle and maple leaves, and matched-view reference photos from the exact Bed close-up, Front and Tree-in-lawn eye positions.
problems.problem:
3 h does not fit what the bake-off asks for:
- The renders are judged in Day and Golden hour, so matched references need at least two sun conditions, and therefore two visits.
- The subjects are at different sites: nursery or client stock for Smaragd and Annabelle, a lawn tree for the maple.
- The synthesis's own rate is 1-1.5 h per species per visit before any reference photos, which is already 3-4.5 h for three species.
problems.evidence:
Synthesis route 2: 'Owner shooting about 1-1.5 h per species per season visit'. The bake-off cameras_and_modes section specifies 'Day and Golden hour'.

If RBG were used as a site, https://www.rbg.ca/photography/ says 'A permit is required for any professional photography done at RBG', at $172-375 plus HST.
problems.fix: Budget two owner sessions (midday and golden hour), about 5-7 h in total, plus travel. Name the sites and the permission needed before scheduling.

problems.claim: Verdict: 'A homeowner will not be able to tell DeckCraft plants from a photo ... in Photo-mode stills'. Optional gate: 5-10 homeowners, 10 pairs, 'Target: no better than 60% correct identification.'
problems.problem:
The test cannot support the claim:
- 60% correct is above the 50% chance level, so the stated pass threshold allows homeowners to tell the difference.
- The sample is too small and its trials are correlated, so plants that are clearly identifiable would often still pass.
problems.evidence:
With 5-10 judges x 10 pairs, there are 50-100 correlated trials. If the true identification rate is 65%:
- n=100: P(observed <= 60%) is about 0.17;
- n=50: P(observed <= 60%) is about 0.28.
(Normal approximation to the binomial.)
problems.fix: Either reword the verdict to 'rarely distinguishable', or use a two-alternative forced-choice test with at least 200 trials and report a 95% confidence interval. Pass only if the interval includes 50% and its upper bound is at most about 60%.

problems.claim: Browser-AI atlas sheets: 'in the only expert study (Theidel, JoDLA 11-2026 ...) botany and geometry scored 2.21/5 and trustworthiness 1.57/5'. This is used to judge single leaf and flower atlas sheets.
problems.problem: The paper measures something different from AI-generated leaf or flower atlas sheets, so the evidence is mis-scoped. Its findings support caution about whole AI planting renders, not the quality of atlas sheets.
problems.fix: Cite it as weak, indirect evidence from one GPT-4o whole-scene image rated by seven experts. Rely on the bake-off's own blind test of an AI atlas sheet, and drop 'the only expert study' unless that is verified.
